name: Commercial greenhouse
summary: Gutter-connected poly/polycarbonate or glass production greenhouse with heating, cooling, ventilation, irrigation and controls, priced per SF of growing-house footprint. Cost spans an order of magnitude: single-bay poly Quonset houses run ~$9–10/SF, wholesale gutter-connected houses ~$20/SF installed, retail and high-tech glass houses with lighting $40–60+/SF. Public data are mostly manufacturer/extension anecdotes (no cost-consultant benchmarks found), so confidence is medium-low.

typicalSize.method: Low 10,000 SF ≈ two-house small grower (MSU recommends ≥5,500 SF for a one-person business, e1); mid ~100,000 SF (≈2.3 acres) regional wholesale/produce grower; e4 cites wholesale projects of 37,800 and 181,440 SF; high ≈ 23 acres for large hydroponic produce operations.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Greenhouse footprint covers ~55–80% of the site after headhouse, loading, stormwater, roads and setbacks: 43,560 × 0.55–0.80.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Production staff ≈ 1 worker per 5,000–10,000 SF; retail garden-center greenhouses need more (≈1 per 2,000 SF → high).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Installed greenhouse + systems: e4 wholesale gutter-connected projects $14–18/SF materials, 'under $20/SF' with labor; e2 Prospiant $10/SF structure rising to $20–30/SF fully outfitted; e3 Fixr commercial $25–35/SF; e4 retail gutter-connected $41–45/SF materials. Typical production house with heating/cooling/irrigation/benches ≈ $25/SF (midpoint of e2 outfitted range and e3 low end) + ~25% for GC/OH&P, site grading, gravel/partial concrete floors, drainage and on-site utilities ≈ $32/SF. Low $15 = e1 basic Quonset $8.60/SF (2019, owner-assisted, no site prep) grossed up for contractor install and sitework. High $60 = high-tech glass with supplemental lighting/retail (e4 $41–45 materials + labor). Evidence years 2019–2025 (e1 2019, e3 2022, e2/e4 2025 publications); stated in 2024$ without index escalation — verify.

scope.notes: Greenhouse structure and glazing, heating, ventilation/evaporative cooling, irrigation/fertigation, benches or floor growing, controls, electrical, footings/curbs, grading, gravel/concrete floors, on-site utilities, GC/OH&P. Excludes supplemental grow lighting (optional line), headhouse building (line item), land, off-site utilities, soft costs.

qualityTiers.method: Economy ≈ low/mid ($15/$32, poly hoop/Quonset — e1, e3 hoop $5–10/SF); premium ≈ polycarbonate or glass gutter-connected with energy curtains; luxury ≈ high/mid ($60/$32) high-tech glass or retail conservatory (e4).

systemSplit.method: Anchored on e1 MSU itemized Quonset budget: frame + double poly cover = 25% of total, fans/shutters/heaters/HAF/thermostats = 35%, cooling pads + irrigation 12%, benches 11%. For a contractor-built gutter-connected house: greenhouse structure, glazing, shade/energy curtains and vents (MasterFormat 13 34 13 glazed structures) 0.43; heating/ventilation/cooling 23 = 0.12; irrigation/fertigation and water 22 = 0.06; benches/growing systems 11 = 0.10; electrical 26 = 0.06; environmental controls 25 = 0.02; footings/curbs/floors 03 = 0.06; sitework 31/32/33 = 0.08; general conditions 01 = 0.07. Proportions are estimates (verify).

lineItems.name: Growing benches (metal frame, movable tops)

cost.method: e1: wood bench frames with mesh tops $1.50/SF of bench; metal-frame movable benches 'starting at $3 per square foot' (can cost more than triple wood). Qty = 64% bench-to-floor ratio per e1. High assumed for rolling/ebb-and-flood benches.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out; floor-grown crops or hydroponic gutters replace benches.

lineItems.name: Supplemental LED grow lighting

cost.method: Assumption: ~15–40 W/SF installed LED top-lighting at roughly $0.35–0.50 per installed watt including power distribution. Not sourced — verify with fixture quote and utility rebate.

lineItems.notes: Common for year-round leafy greens/tomatoes in northern latitudes.

lineItems.name: Headhouse / packing & work building (≈10% of greenhouse area)

cost.method: Pre-engineered metal building with slab, restrooms, cooler/packing area, priced like light-industrial/agricultural buildings ($60–160/SF). Area ratio 5–15% of greenhouse assumed. Verify.

lineItems.notes: Most commercial operations need one; set qty to 0 if existing.

lineItems.name: Energy / blackout curtain system

cost.method: Assumption: motorized curtain systems in gutter-connected houses. Not sourced — verify.

lineItems.notes: Often in premium tier; reduces heating cost ~20–30%.

lineItems.name: Water well and LP gas storage (where no utility service)

cost.method: e1 notes cost increases if a water well and LP gas tanks are needed (no value given). Amount assumed. Verify locally.

pctOfHard.method: Greenhouses are largely manufacturer-engineered packages (design included in the kit) with agricultural permitting; soft costs below commercial-building norms (≈15–25%). Mid 10% = site/civil engineering, permits, structural stamp, PM, builder's risk.

softCosts.notes: Agricultural building exemptions in some states reduce permit cost.

design.method: Pre-engineered package; design risk mainly site/civil and utilities.

hard.method: Typical agricultural/pre-engineered construction; higher for remote sites and steel price volatility.

perPrimaryUnit.method: All-in hard + soft (excl. land): $10/SF hoop-style production house up to ~$90/SF high-tech glass with lighting and headhouse.

evidence.quote: The construction cost in 2019 for this type of greenhouse, fully assembled, is $24,770 or $8.60 per square foot. (Table 1: 30-by-96-foot, double-layered polyethylene, Quonset-style greenhouse, 2,880 sq. ft.; land cost and site preparation are not included)
evidence.scopeNotes: Single-bay poly Quonset with fans, gas heaters, cooling pads, drip irrigation, wood benches; installation at 90 hr × $16/hr (owner-assisted); excludes site prep and land. Low-end bound.

source.title: How Much Does a Commercial Greenhouse Cost?

evidence.quote: For example, a $10 per square foot structure may rise to $20-$30 per square foot when fully outfitted with advanced systems. ... installation costs ... run as much as two times higher than the material and equipment costs alone.
evidence.scopeNotes: Vendor marketing page (published 2022, updated Dec 2025); scope of figures not defined.

source.title: How much does it cost to build a greenhouse?

evidence.quote: Commercial greenhouses cost around $25 to $35 a square foot on average ... Hoop greenhouses cost between $5 and $10 a square foot on average.
evidence.scopeNotes: Consumer cost-guide figure (updated Aug 2022); scope unclear.

evidence.region: United States (project examples; one in rural Wisconsin)

source.title: Looking at the cost of running a greenhouse

evidence.quote: Zephyr Wholesale (37,800 sq ft): 'The cost breakdown is $14 per square foot for materials' (under $20/SF incl. labor); Dual Atriums (181,440 sq ft): 'close to $18 per square foot'; Gutter-Connected Vail retail (6,600 sq ft): 'close to $45 per square foot'.
evidence.scopeNotes: Manufacturer project examples, mostly materials only, build years not stated (article March 2025).

openQuestions: No cost-consultant or public-bid data found for large (5–30 acre) hydroponic glass greenhouses; public company filings (e.g., produce CEA growers) would anchor the high end.
University enterprise budgets (Penn State, Cornell, UMass) for gutter-connected houses were not retrieved this session (web search budget exhausted).
Supplemental lighting, headhouse and curtain costs are assumptions.
